RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Skyler Brooks
Member ID: W708133981
Reference Number: POC-7572D3C32F-37314
Requested Service: Partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446
Date of Notice: 2026-08-06
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-02

To the Aetna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-06 (Reference No. POC-7572D3C32F-37314). The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that Aetna reverse this determination based on the clinical record summarized below and on Aetna's own published medical-necessity criteria for this procedure.

**Governing Policy**

Based on my research, Aetna applies Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) Number 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty," to prior authorization requests for CPT 27446 (available at https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html). I was not able to confirm the effective or last-revised date of the version of this policy applied to my request from the publicly available page. I ask that Aetna identify, in its response to this appeal, the exact version and effective date of CPB 0660 that was used to make this determination, and provide a copy if it differs from the current publicly posted text quoted below.

**Response to the Stated Denial Reason (Imaging)**

The stated basis for denial was that submitted imaging did not support medical necessity. CPB 0660 states, as one of the necessity criteria for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, that the member must have:

"Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) ... affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").

The MRI of the knee performed on 2026-06-02 documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 changes limited to the medial compartment. This finding meets the plain language of the imaging criterion quoted above. I ask that Aetna's clinical reviewer re-examine this MRI report against this specific criterion, and if the denial rested on a misreading of the study or an incomplete copy of the report, that the file be corrected and the determination reversed. If Aetna's review team relied on additional imaging-related sub-criteria not disclosed in the denial notice (for example, ligament stability or range-of-motion findings on imaging or exam), I ask that these be specified in writing so that my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, can supply the corresponding documentation.

**Mapping of the Clinical Record to CPB 0660 Medical-Necessity Criteria**

1. Pain and functional disability interfering with ADLs
CPB 0660 requires: "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: I have had 12 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain, both of which represent clear interference with activities of daily living.

2. Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion/swelling on exam
CPB 0660 requires: "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

3. Ligament stability
CPB 0660 requires: "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: [Ligament stability examination findings, e.g., Lachman/anterior drawer results, are not included in the clinical summary provided to me — Dr. Lindqvist can supply this documentation.]

4. Knee arc of motion
CPB 0660 requires: "Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: [Specific range-of-motion measurement in degrees is not included in the clinical summary provided to me — Dr. Lindqvist can supply the goniometric measurement confirming this criterion is met.]

5. Radiographic evidence of single-compartment moderate/severe osteoarthritis
CPB 0660 requires: "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) ... affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: MRI dated 2026-06-02 shows full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment and Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 changes isolated to that compartment. This criterion is met.

6. History of unsuccessful conservative therapy, including formal physical therapy
CPB 0660 requires: "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: I completed 16 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (2026-03-09 to 2026-06-29, 16 visits) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. My BMI is 29 (below the 40 threshold that would trigger the longer 24-week requirement). This 16-week supervised PT course exceeds the applicable 12-week threshold.

7. Required elements of conservative therapy
CPB 0660 further specifies that conservative therapy must include, unless contraindicated: "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications ... to joint replacement, optional for others); and Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications ... to joint replacement, optional for others)" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy addressing flexibility and strengthening, and received a corticosteroid (therapeutic) injection on 2026-04-08 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief, despite which my ADLs remained diminished. [Documentation of specific activity-modification counseling and any assistive device use, if applicable, is not included in the clinical summary provided to me and can be supplied by Dr. Lindqvist if needed.] Because my BMI is 29 and I do not fall into the relative-contraindication category described in the policy (BMI greater than 40, or age less than 50 — [age not stated in the records provided to me]), assistive device use and therapeutic injection were optional rather than required elements, but I nonetheless completed a therapeutic injection.

8. Absence of contraindications to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
CPB 0660 states the member must have "none of the following contraindications to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: Previous proximal tibial osteotomy or distal femoral osteotomy; or Tibial or femoral shaft deformity; or Radiographic evidence of medial or lateral subluxation; or Flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees; or Varus deformity greater than 15 degrees (medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty) or a valgus deformity greater than 20 degrees (lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty); or Inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy; or Subchondral bone loss due to large subchondral cysts or extensive focal osteonecrosis" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: [The clinical summary provided to me does not explicitly document the absence of each of these specific findings — Dr. Lindqvist can confirm on the record that none of these contraindications are present.]

9. Absence of absolute contraindications to joint replacement
CPB 0660 states the member must have none of the following: "Active infection of the joint or active systemic bacteremia that has not been totally eradicated; or Active skin infection ... or open wound within the planned surgical site of the knee; or Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty; or Vascular insufficiency, significant muscular atrophy of the leg, or neuromuscular disease severe enough to compromise implant stability or post-operative recovery or quadriplegia; or Osseous abnormalities that cannot be optimally managed ...; or Allergy to components of the implant" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: There is no active infection. Regarding the corticosteroid injection contraindication: my injection was administered on 2026-04-08. [The planned date of surgery is not stated in the records provided to me; please confirm that the scheduled surgical date is more than 12 weeks after 2026-04-08 so that this criterion is clearly satisfied.]

10. Diabetes-related additional note
CPB 0660 states: "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty" (Aetna CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty").
Record: [Diabetic status and, if applicable, most recent HbA1c value are not included in the clinical summary provided to me. If I am not diabetic, this criterion is not applicable; Dr. Lindqvist can confirm.]

**Requested Action**

I ask that Aetna reverse the denial of CPT 27446 and approve the requested partial knee replacement, based on the medical record summarized above, which substantially satisfies the medical-necessity criteria in CPB 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty," particularly the imaging criterion that was cited as the basis for denial. In the alternative, if Aetna's reviewers believe specific documentation is still missing (for example, ligament-stability testing, exact range-of-motion measurements, or confirmation of the absence of structural contraindications), I ask that Aetna identify exactly which criterion or sub-criterion remains unmet so that Dr. Lindqvist can submit the corresponding records promptly, within the applicable appeal window.

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice (deadline 2027-02-02).

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected timeframe for a decision. If additional records, an authorized representative form, or a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Lindqvist would assist in this review, please contact [provider office contact name and phone number] or me directly at the number/email above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Skyler Brooks
Member ID: W708133981
